seoTitle: Free xxHash, MurmurHash3, FNV-1a and SipHash Online
metaDescription: Compute xxHash32 and 64, MurmurHash3, FNV-1 and FNV-1a, and SipHash with a seed or key. Fast non-cryptographic hashes, free in your browser.
intro: Enter data as text, hex or base64, choose a hash and optionally set a seed or SipHash key. The tool returns the value in hex and decimal.
why: Hash tables, bloom filters, sharding keys, deduplication and content-based caches rely on fast hashes that are not meant to be secure. xxHash, MurmurHash3, FNV-1a and SipHash show up in databases, compilers, languages and network software, and ports to other languages are a regular source of subtle bugs: wrong seed handling, byte order or a missing final mix. This page lets you check your implementation against a known-good one for the same input and seed. SipHash accepts a 128-bit key and is designed to protect hash tables against collision attacks, though it is still not a general-purpose cryptographic hash. The others should never be used to protect data or store passwords. The calculation runs in your browser.
howTo: Enter the data and choose text, hex or base64.
Pick the algorithm and, if needed, set the seed or the 32-hex-character SipHash key.
Read the result in hex and decimal.

faq.a: No. xxHash, MurmurHash3 and FNV are built for speed and distribution, and collisions are easy to craft. SipHash is a keyed function that suits hash tables but is not a general cryptographic hash.
As a decimal number or 0x hexadecimal value. xxHash32 and MurmurHash3 use the lower 32 bits, xxHash64 uses 64 bits. FNV has no seed, and SipHash uses the key.
A 128-bit key as 32 hex characters. The default 000102...0f is the one used in the SipHash reference test vectors.
xxHash32 and xxHash64, MurmurHash3 x86 32-bit, FNV-1 and FNV-1a in 32 and 64 bits, and SipHash-2-4 and SipHash-1-3.
